anya: idea: edge emits a short-lived 'guardian-fp' claim for fairness mapping. goal: stable bucket w/o PII.
mike: sounds good. signed claim or raw hash?
anya: prefer signed HMAC claim from managed edge, fallback to unsigned hash for telemetry. ttl ~30m.
sam: threat model: header spoofing and rapid churn. signed claim + exp helps. also need verify cache.
lina: security: require ingress auth and HMAC kids per-region. admission verifies sigs; cache positive results to avoid HSM per-request. :lock:
mike: proto boundary: admission accepts either `guardian_fp` (string) or `guardian_fp_claim` (base64). quota-only trusts claim. keep admit payload tiny.
sam: metrics: `guardian.fp.verify.ok`, `.bad_sig`, `.expired`, `quota.map.from_fp` and `abuse.fp.churn_rate`.
anya: fallback policy: signed+valid -> deterministic bucket; missing/invalid -> tag `fp=untrusted` and apply conservative softcap. control-plane KMS outage -> fall back to unsigned smoothing.
lina: privacy: never store raw ip/ua, only hashed fp. retention: telemetry 30d, signed audit 90d. opt-out via `X-RW-FP-OPT-OUT`.
mike: rollout plan: telemetry-only -> canary signed claims -> pilot enforcement for premium tenants -> wider enforcement. feature-flag per-tenant.
sam: I'll build churn detectors and synthetic tests. lina: I'll draft security checklist. mike: RFC for proto + cache semantics. anya: I'll own rollout playbook.
deploy-bot: canary deploy: guardian-fp-v1 -> region=us-west canary=5%.
anya: thanks all. follow-ups in RFC thread. :eyes:
